digest.component_or_area: graph link store and inbound reconciler
propositions: Link writes are relation-scoped per (target_id, relation) so one pair can hold multiple relations (blocks and relates_to simultaneously), but removal is pair-scoped and takes no relation argument, causing permanent non-convergence when a pair holds two relations and one is deleted by a peer.

The inbound reconciler's guard G5 in _inbound_unlink_one declines removal when the pair's most-recent net-active relation does not match the peer-deleted relation, and this decline is permanent because the removal record re-emits and re-declines on every pass.

Direction-agnostic deduplication of outbound ADD on (vendor_type, target_key) without relation matching causes outbound re-adds to be skipped for double-related pairs, preventing guard G4 suppression and allowing removal records to reach G5.

The fix introduces relation-scoped removal at the graph layer (remove_dependency) symmetric with add_dependency, making the reconciler's inbound removal converge by removing exactly the mirrored relation instead of declining.

The CLI and library facade gain optional relation arguments (rebar unlink <id1> <id2> [relation]) that are backward-compatible; with no relation the existing pair-scoped most-recent behavior is unchanged.
Removal naming a relation with no matching net-active local link removes nothing and is a logged no-op, preserving the safety invariant that no link the peer still carries is ever removed.
